content: Following a separation, a wife sought half the value of a pastry shop founded during the marriage. The husband contended it was an enterprise managed solely by him, where the wife only had a participation in profits. The Court ruled that under the legal community regime, assets of a business formed during marriage fall into the comunione de residuo upon dissolution. The wife was therefore entitled to 50% of the net equity value and the goodwill (avviamento), as these represent the accumulated fruits of the marital partnership regardless of who managed the enterprise.
